Mikael Staffas
(President and [[chief executive officer|CEO]]) | industry = [[Metal]]s and [[Mining]] | products = [[Copper]], [[zinc]], [[nickel]], [[lead]], [[precious metals]], [[sulphuric acid]], [[Platinum group|PGM]], [[iron sand]] | revenue = {{Decrease}} {{SEK|78.554 billion|link=yes}} (2023) | operating_income = {{Decrease}} {{SEK|8.287 billion}} (2023) | net_income = {{Decrease}} {{SEK|6.074 billion}} (2023) | assets = {{Increase}} {{SEK|101.957 billion}} (2023) | equity = {{Decrease}} {{SEK|56.420 billion}} (2023) | num_employees = {{Decrease}} 5,664 (2023) | website = {{URL|https://www.boliden.com}} }} '''Boliden AB''' (stylized as '''Boliden''') is a [[Sweden|Swedish]] multinational metals, mining, and [[smelting]] company headquartered in [[Stockholm]]. The company produces [[zinc]], [[copper]], [[lead]], [[nickel]], [[silver]], and [[gold]], with operations in Sweden, Finland, Norway, Portugal, and Ireland. Founded in the 1920s and named after the Boliden mine, a now-defunct gold mine 30 km northwest of the Swedish town of [[Skellefteå]], Boliden AB began as a gold mining company. Over the following decades, it expanded into copper, silver and nickel mining, as well as smelting. In the 1970s, following a period of high metals prices, the company diversified aggressively, purchasing [[Major appliance|appliance]] manufacturers, [[Wholesaling|wholesalers]] and [[Trading company|trading companies]]. In 1985, it was [[Takeover|acquired]] by [[Trelleborg (company)|Trelleborg]], a [[polymer]] manufacturer, which refocused it back on mining while also expanding overseas. In 1998, Trelleborg moved Boliden's headquarters to Toronto, Canada and sold Boliden again on the stock market. However, Boliden's [[share price]] collapsed over the next four years, due to a combination of low metal prices and a [[dam failure]] at one of its mines in Spain that [[Doñana disaster|led to an environmental disaster]]. In 2002, it moved its headquarters back to Sweden, sold off its non-European assets and regained profitability. Boliden owns and operates Europe's biggest zinc mine at [[Tara Mine|Tara]] in Ireland (acquired in 2004). Boliden also owns [[:sv:Garpenbergs gruva|Garpenberg]], a zinc-lead mine and Sweden's oldest mine still in operation. The mineral-rich Skellefte field lies within the Boliden Area, where almost 30 mines have been opened since production began in the 1920s and where Boliden currently operates the Renström and Kristineberg underground mines and the Maurliden open pit mine. Boliden also owns and operates the [[Aitik]] copper mine. Boliden refines both [[Ore concentrate|metal concentrate]] and scrap waste at its smelters in Sweden, Finland and Norway to produce [[base metal]]s and [[precious metal]]s. Its main metals are zinc and copper, but the production of lead, gold and silver also makes a substantial contribution to its revenues. It is also a significant producer of [[sulfuric acid]] as a refining byproduct. == Operations ==

=== Mines === Boliden is active in mining, [[Refining (metallurgy)|refining]], [[smelting]] and [[Chemical plant|chemical production]]. As of 2025, Boliden operates seven mines, all of them in Europe (see table).{{Cite news |title=Tara Mines owner Boliden tops earnings estimates in first quarter |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/business/2025/04/23/tara-mines-owner-boliden-tops-earnings-estimates-in-first-quarter/ |access-date=2025-07-26 |newspaper=The Irish Times |language=en}} Its mining activities are primarily in [[Zinc mining|zinc]] and [[Copper extraction|copper]], as well as some lead, [[Gold mining|gold]], [[Silver mining|silver]].{{Cite web |last1=Strömbäck |first1=Alexandra |last2=Ivarsson |first2=Oskar |year=2015 |title=Boliden - one of the world's largest mining and smelting companies - North Sweden |url=https://www.northsweden.eu/english/news/2015/boliden-one-of-the-worlds-largest-mining-and-smelting-companies/ |access-date=2025-07-26 |website=[[North Sweden European Office]]}} The mines are geographically concentrated in Sweden, but the company also operates a mine each in Finland, Ireland and Portugal. Its most productive mine in 2024 was Aitik producing 41 million tonnes of ore, followed by Kevitsa, with 10 million tonnes.{{Cite press release |title=Boliden: Mineral Resources and Mineral Reserves 2024 |url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/boliden-mineral-resources-and-mineral-reserves-2024-302369822.html |access-date=2025-07-26 |website=www.prnewswire.com |language=en |type=Press release}} Aitik is Europe's fourth-biggest copper mine{{Cite web |year=2021 |title=Europe: Five Largest Copper Mines in 2021 |url=https://www.globaldata.com/data-insights/mining/europe--five-largest-copper-mines-in-2090652/ |website=Global Data}} despite having relatively low-grade ore (0.2–0.4%);{{Cite journal |last1=Schmitt |first1=Raoul |last2=Parian |first2=Mehdi |last3=Ghorbani |first3=Yousef |last4=McElroy |first4=I. |year=2022 |title=A geometallurgical approach towards the correlation between rock type mineralogy and grindability: A case study in Aitik mine, Sweden |url=https://urn.kb.se/resolve?urn=urn:nbn:se:ltu:diva-92745 |journal=IMPC Asia-Pacific 2022 Conference Proceedings}} it owes its productivity to its large [[economies of scale]] and high degree of [[automation]]. Boliden spent SEK 929 million [[Swedish krona|SEK]] (US$88 million) on exploration in 2024. === Smelters === Boliden also owns and operates five [[Smelting|smelters]].{{Cite web |last=Olsson |first=Elin |date=2017-09-20 |title=Nya chefen: "Vi tjänar mer pengar än någonsin" |url=https://www.vk.se/2017-09-20/nya-chefen-vi-tjanar-mer-pengar-an-nagonsin |access-date=2025-07-29 |website=Västerbottens-Kuriren |language=sv}} [[Rönnskär]], Boliden's oldest smelter, is located in northern Sweden and produces primarily copper and sulfuric acid, as well as some lead and zinc. Norzinc, a smelter in [[Odda (town)|Odda]], Norway, produces zinc and sulfuric acid. Bergsöe, a lead smelter in the southern Swedish town of [[Landskrona]], is a [[Lead–acid battery|lead-acid battery]] recycling plant.{{Cite book |last=Lehner |first=Theo |chapter=Integrated recycling of non-ferrous metals at Boliden LTD. Ronnskar smelter |date=1998 |title=Proceedings of the 1998 IEEE International Symposium on Electronics and the Environment. ISEE - 1998 (Cat. No.98CH36145) |publisher=IEEE |pages=42–47 |doi=10.1109/ISEE.1998.675028 |isbn=978-0-7803-4295-8}} A smelter in [[Harjavalta]] in southern Finland chiefly produces copper and nickel, as well as minor amounts of gold, silver and palladium. A smelter in [[Kokkola]], northern Finland, produces zinc.{{Cite book |url=https://investors.boliden.com/sites/boliden-ir/files/files/annual-report/2-Operations_Boliden-Annual-and-Sustainability-Report-2023.pdf |title=Boliden Annual and Sustainability Report 2023 |date=February 2024 |language=en}} Kokkola is specialized in the production of "special high-grade zinc", which is used in [[galvanization]].{{Cite web |last=Liukkonen |first=Sini |year=2015 |title=Tietojärjestelmät osaamisen johtamisessa |url=http://www.theseus.fi/handle/10024/91001 |access-date=2025-07-29 |publisher=Centria University of Applied Sciences}} The Odda zinc smelter, which produces zinc for the steel industry and aluminium fluoride for Norway's aluminium industry, is located on the west coast of Norway. The [[Rönnskär]] copper smelter also produces metals from electronic scrap and other secondary materials. The Harjavalta copper smelter, located on the west coast of Finland, produces copper cathodes that are mainly sold to manufacturers of semi-finished goods. Bergsöe is one of Europe's four biggest players in the lead recycling industry. Approximately 60% of the plant's lead production is sold to the European battery industry, with the remainder used in the manufacture of roofing sheet. Only around 40–50% of the raw materials Boliden refines at its smelters are from its own mines. Most of the remainder is sourced from other mining companies. 5–10% of its raw copper, nickel and zinc, as well as 60% of its raw lead feed, is from recycling scrap. ==History== === 1920s: founding === [[File:Oscar Falkman direktör.jpg|thumb|190x190px|Oscar Falkman, early investor and first CEO of Boliden AB]] [[File:Boliden 1939 SMDIG00172.jpg|thumb|The Boliden mine (right) and adjoining town (left) in 1939]] In 1918, a mining company called ''Centralgruppens Emissionsbolag'', which was majority-owned by [[Skandinaviska Banken|Skaninaviska Banken]], began prospecting in the area surrounding [[Skellefteå]]. In 1924, a gold ore deposit was discovered near the village of Bjurliden, around 30 km from Skellefteå. It was found to contain 18 grams of gold per ton, making it Europe's richest ore at the time.{{Cite journal |last1=Weihed |first1=Jeanette Bergman |last2=Bergstrom |first2=Ulf |last3=Billstrom |first3=Kjell |last4=Weihed |first4=Par |date=1996-10-01 |title=Geology, tectonic setting, and origin of the Paleoproterozoic Boliden Au-Cu-As deposit, Skellefte District, northern Sweden |url=http://pubs.geoscienceworld.org/economicgeology/article/91/6/1073/21662/Geology-tectonic-setting-and-origin-of-the |journal=Economic Geology |language=en |volume=91 |issue=6 |pages=1073–1097 |doi=10.2113/gsecongeo.91.6.1073 |bibcode=1996EcGeo..91.1073W |issn=1554-0774}} It also contained significant amounts of silver and copper.{{Cite book |last1=Wiklund |first1=Roine |url=https://umu.diva-portal.org/smash/record.jsf?pid=diva2:1900483 |title=Det nya framtidslandet? |last2=Linkmark |first2=Magnus |last3=Bergquist |first3=Ann-Kristin |work=Historisk Tidskrift |publisher=Umeå universitet |year=2024 |volume=144 |issue=3 |page=522 |language=SV |trans-title=The new land of the future?}} In the mid-1920s, the company went bankrupt. Its main [[shareholder]] Skaninaviska Banken [[Liquidation|liquidated]] and restructured it into two separate companies, retaining majority ownership of both: ''Skellefteå gruv AB'' and ''Västerbottens gruv AB.'' Oscar Falkman, a [[venture capital]]ist who had led Emissionsbolag's [[prospecting]] operations since 1918, became the leader of both companies. Financier [[Ivar Kreuger]] bought majority shares in both companies in 1929 for 58 million [[Swedish krona|SEK]] ({{Inflation|index=SE|value=0.058|start_year=1929|r=1}} billion SEK today, or 183 million [[Euro|EUR]]){{Cite web |last=Fagerfjäll |first=Ronald |date=2025-05-01 |title=Livet efter Kreuger |url=https://www.bizstories.se/naringslivet/livet-efter-kreuger/ |access-date=2025-06-11 |website=Bizstories |language=sv-SE}} and two years later consolidated them into one, which became the modern entity Boliden.{{Cite journal |last=Bergquist |first=Ann-Kristin |date=2017 |title=The Swedish nonferrous mining industry and the environmental issue. The case of Boliden business archives |url=https://shs.cairn.info/journal-entreprises-et-histoire-2017-1-page-157 |journal=Entreprises et histoire |language=en |volume=86 |issue=1 |pages=157–159 |doi=10.3917/eh.086.0157 |issn=1161-2770}} Falkman became its first [[Chief executive officer|CEO]], ultimately serving for 12 years.{{Cite web |title=Oscar Falkman |url=https://www.ne.se/uppslagsverk/encyklopedi/l%C3%A5ng/oscar-falkman |work=[[Nationalencyklopedin]]}} === 1930s–1940s: restructuring and expansion === In 1932, Kreuger, who was heavily indebted and facing bankruptcy, died of suicide. The Swedish government passed a law limiting foreign ownership of Swedish companies active in resource extraction. The law, dubbed ''Lex Boliden'' by the press, remained on the books until the 1990s.{{Cite web |last=Insändarredaktionen |date=2013-01-23 |title=Åter till lex Boliden |url=https://www.norran.se/insandare/not-found/artikel/ater-till-lex-boliden/lym9mn7l |access-date=2025-06-25 |website=Norran |language=sv}} Ultimately, Kreuger's stake in Boliden passed back to Skandinaviska Banken, which had provided most of the money for his purchase of the mine. The bank remained the owners of the company until 1952, when the company shares were publicly listed.{{Cite web |last=Myhr |first=Karin Jansson |date=2025-05-16 |title=Boliden - över 100 år sedan det stora guldfyndet |url=https://www.bizstories.se/foretagen/det-stora-guldfyndet-som-forandrade-allt/ |access-date=2025-06-24 |website=Bizstories |language=sv-SE}} Over the next few years, the town of [[Boliden]] grew quickly around the mine. ==== Smelting operations ==== In 1930, Boliden commissioned a [[Smelting|smelter]] in the coastal town of [[Skelleftehamn]] to process the Boliden ore. The site saw significant expansion in the rest of the 20th century and is today part of the company's [[Rönnskär]] factory. In the 1940s, Boliden began producing purified [[lead]], [[silver]] and [[arsenic]] there. In 1952, the company began to produce [[Sulfuric acid|sulphuric acid]] from its own [[Sulfur dioxide|sulphur dioxide]] emissions. In 1970, a dedicated refinery was built to concentrate and purify the sulphur dioxide to increase the recovery rate. Boliden had a near-[[monopoly]] on sulphuric acid in Sweden at that time.{{Cite book |last=Bergquist |first=Ann-Kristin |url=https://www.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:140796/FULLTEXT01.pdf |title=Guld och Gröna Skogar? Miljöanpassningen av Rönnskärsverken 1960-2000 |date=October 19, 2007 |publisher=Umeå University |type=PhD Thesis}} ==== Diversification beyond gold ==== [[File:Linbanan Kristineberg-Boliden (1943).jpg|thumb|Aerial tramway between Kristineberg and Boliden (1943)]]Responding to demand created by the war economies of World War II, Boliden began investing in the [[Copper extraction|extraction]] and processing of [[copper]], as well as some [[lead]] and [[nickel]]. The company commissioned the [[Laver (ghost town)|Laver]] copper mine in 1936, which was only operational for ten years. The following year,{{Cite web |last=Lundström |first=Gunnar |date=April 1996 |title=Kristineberg: från glesbygd till modernt gruvsamhälle |url=https://underjordskyrkan.se/info/kristineberg.pdf |access-date=2025-06-24 |website=underjordskyrkan.se}} Boliden also bought a significant amount of land near [[Kristineberg, Lycksele|Kristineberg]] from local prospector and miner Johan Alfred Hultdin for 50,000 SEK (1.9 million SEK today, or 170,000 EUR). The company quickly developed the site and commissioned mining operations in 1940. In 1943, the company began operating a 96-kilometre [[aerial tramway]] between Kristineberg and Boliden for the transportation of ore.{{Cite news |last=Huggert |first=Anders |date=1994 |editor-last=Lundgren |editor-first=Britta |title=Guldriket |url=https://vbm.se/vbmstorage/uploads/2017/09/1994_1.pdf |access-date=2025-06-24 |work=Västerbotten |page=18}} In 1943, Boliden opened a lead mine in [[Laisvall]] that was active until 2001. === 1950s–1980: zinc and lead === Boliden began expanding its lead production and also investing in [[zinc]], which together made up the majority of the company's metal output by the 1960s. In 1957, Boliden acquired the company ''Zinkgruvor AB,'' taking over its mines in the [[Bergslagen]] region, including a zinc and silver mine at [[Garpenberg]]{{Cite web | url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/248475866 | title=Garpenberg––an old concentrator at peak performance | first1=Nils-Johan | last1=Bolin | first2=P. | last2=Brodin | first3=P. | last3=Lampinen | work=Minerals Engineering | via=[[ResearchGate]] | date=November 2003}} and [[Långfallsgruvan]], a zinc mine near [[Saxberget]]. Boliden opened the [[Aitik|Aitik mine]], an [[Open-pit mining|open pit mine]] copper mine, near [[Gällivare]] in 1968.{{Cite book |last1=Eriksson |first1=Nils |url=https://gallivare.se/download/18.4e20a890188bda337d11eb12/1687109181794/MKB%20avseende%20%C3%B6kad%20produktion%2020121218.pdf |title=Aitikgruvan: Miljökonsekvensbeskrivning avseende ökad produktion, höjning av sand- och klarningsmagasin m.m. |last2=Lindeström |first2=Lennart |date=2012-12-18 |language=SV |trans-title=Aitik mine: Environmental impact assessment regarding increased production, raising of sand and clarification reservoirs, etc.}} The company also continued producing gold, as well as silver, arsenic, selenium, nickel sulphate, zinc, and sulphuric acid. In the 1960s, Boliden began to develop processes to refine complex metal mixtures, critical for recycling industrial [[scrap]]. The company was one of the key developers of the [[Kaldo converter|Kaldo furnace]] to treat lead-containing copper. In 1967, the original Boliden mine was closed down.{{Cite web |title=From Past to Present |url=https://www.boliden.com/globalassets/about-boliden/bolidens-history/337-5365-historisk-folder_2014_en_3.pdf |publisher=Boliden AB}}[[File:Aitik coppar mine 1.JPG|thumb|Boliden opened the [[Aitik|Aitik copper mine]] in 1968.]] In 1973, Boliden acquired half of the lead mining operations of the German company Preussag (today [[TUI Group]]). Boliden aimed to expand its [[lead smelting]] and refining capacity, as well as facilitate the sale of its lead products. The deal also marked Boliden's first major entry into markets outside of Sweden. In 1976, Boliden launched a [[Kaldo converter|Kaldo type furnace]], for processing metals. 1976 also saw Boliden launch the first [[flash smelting]] furnace for lead, applying Kaldo technology, at [[Rönnskär]]. In 1979, Boliden acquired [[:sv:Bergsöe|Paul Bergsöe & Son]], a Danish smelting company with operations in [[Landskrona]],{{Cite news |last=Andersson |first=Bosse |date=2017 |title=Vart tar alla blybatterier vägen? |url=https://modernaverkstaden.se/wp-content/uploads/2017/10/Reortage-blybatterier-DMV-5-2017.pdf |access-date=2025-06-24 |work=Den Moderna Verkstaden}} which is today primarily a [[Lead–acid battery|lead-acid battery]] recycler.{{Cite book |last=Gustafsson |first=Lotta |url=https://www.diva-portal.org/smash/record.jsf?pid=diva2%3A1234528&dswid=7272 |title=Blytak |date=1999 |publisher=Riksantikvarieämbetet |isbn=978-91-7209-628-8 |location=Stockholm}} === 1980–1986: diversification and acquisition by Trelleborg === By 1980, Boliden was producing around 11 million tonnes of ore per year from 16 mines in central and northern Sweden. Almost all of it was refined at the Rönnskär (Sweden) and [[Odda (town)|Odda]] (Norway). Seeking to diversify its operations, the company expanded aggressively over five years, investing in [[Downstream (manufacturing)|downstream]] activities like [[gallium arsenide]] production and construction materials. It also set up its own materials trading division and, in 1986, purchased the appliance wholesaler [[Ahlsell]] for 1 billion SEK (2.7 billion SEK, or 244 million EUR, in 2025). The acquisition made Boliden one of Sweden's largest companies, with over 15,000 employees. However, by 1985, low international metal prices had severely cut into the company's profits, depressing its share price to the point that it became a target for a [[takeover]].{{Cite journal |last1=Löfkvist |first1=Bengt |last2=Sallert |first2=Mati |date=December 1992 |title=Corporate strategy, location of investments and competitiveness |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/030142079290014Z |journal=Resources Policy |language=en |volume=18 |issue=4 |pages=283–284 |doi=10.1016/0301-4207(92)90014-Z|url-access=subscription }} In 1986, the [[polymer]] manufacturer [[Trelleborg (company)|Trelleborg]] acquired a [[controlling interest]] in Boliden. === 1987–1995: streamlining and international expansion === [[File:Trelleborg company logo.svg|thumb|[[Trelleborg (company)|Trelleborg]] was the majority shareholder of Boliden from 1986 to 1996.]] Trelleborg, Boliden's majority shareholder from 1986 to 1996, initiated a major restructuring of the Boliden Group to refocus the company on its core strengths: mining, mineral refining, and chemicals. A number of unrelated or loss-making subsidiaries totaling over 6,000 employees were sold off, including large parts of the recently purchased Ahlsell, several electronics and [[Major appliance|household appliance]] companies, a number of [[Trading company|trading companies]], and a healthcare provider. The money raised through these divestments were reinvested to expand Boliden's mining operations.{{Cite web |title=Företagsförvärv i svenskt näringsliv |url=https://lagen.nu/sou/1990:1 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220812090412/https://lagen.nu/sou/1990:1 |archive-date=2022-08-12 |access-date=2025-07-16 |website=Lagen.nu}} In particular, Trelleborg aimed to expand Boliden's international footprint, believing that Sweden had become less competitive as a manufacturing location due to [[Taxation in Sweden|high taxes]], stricter environmental laws, and Sweden's lack of membership in the [[European Economic Community]] (a [[single market]] that later grew into the [[European Union]]). The company began acquiring mines outside of Sweden. It opened a Toronto office in 1988. One of the first major international acquisitions was Boliden's purchase of the near-bankrupt zinc and lead mine [[Maamorilik]] in Greenland from [[Cominco]] in 1986.{{Cite journal |last=Thomassen |first=Bjørn |date=April 2003 |title=The Black Angel lead-zinc mine at Maarmorilik in West Greenland |url=https://eng.geus.dk/media/13331/go02_2ed.pdf |journal=Geology and Ore |language=en |publisher=[[Geological Survey of Denmark and Greenland]] |issue=2 |page=5}} The subsequent discovery of further exploitable mineral deposits, combined with the recovery of metals prices in the late 1980s, allowed Boliden to extend the life of the mine by several years at a significant profit. In the same year, Boliden acquired the Spanish company Apirsa, which extracted zinc and lead from the [[Aznalcóllar]] open pit mine, 45 km west of [[Seville]]. The company also redoubled its efforts to finish construction of the Sukhaybarat gold mine in Saudi Arabia, which it had partially acquired several years earlier and was developing as a [[joint venture]] with [[Petromin Corporation|Petromin]]. The mine was finally commissioned in 1991.{{Cite book |last=Khudeira |first=Baker |url=https://ashgill.com.au/pdfs/Sukhaybarat%20Au%20Mine.pdf |title=Sukhaybarat Gold Mine |publisher=Ashgill Australia Pty. Ltd. |language=en}} In 1992, Boliden opened the [[Petiknäs]] zinc mine in northern Sweden after several years of exploration; it was connected to the nearby Rönström zinc/gold mine via a 2.5 km [[Adit|underground passage]] in 1996.{{Cite book |last=Schlatter |first=Denis Martin |url=https://www.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:991328/FULLTEXT01.pdf |title=Volcanic Stratigraphy and Hydrothermal Alteration of the Petiknäs South Zn-Pb-Cu-Au-Ag Volcanic-hosted Massive Sulfide Deposit, Sweden |publisher=Luleå University of Technology |year=2007 |page=7 |language=en}} Some acquisitions proved short-lived. In 1990, Boliden entered a joint venture with [[Burkina Faso|Burkina Faso's]] mining ministry to develop the [[Perkoa]] zinc mine,{{Cite web |date=November 1, 1992 |title=Joint venture between Boliden International Mining and Bureau des Mines et de la Geologie Burkina |url=https://www.thefreelibrary.com/Perkoa+zinc+project,+Burkina+Faso.-a013539012 |access-date=2025-07-20 |website=www.thefreelibrary.com |publisher=Aspermont Media UK |via=thefreelibrary.com}} but withdrew just two years later following a global collapse in zinc prices.{{Cite web |date=2022-10-20 |title=Fermeture de la mine de zinc de Perkoa: Leçons d'un échec |url=https://www.banfora.org/2022/10/20/fermeture-de-la-mine-de-zinc-de-perkoa-lecons-dun-echec/ |access-date=2025-07-20 |website=Amitiés Saintonge Banfora |language=fr}} Similarly, it exited a joint venture{{Cite journal |last=Redwood |first=Stewart D. |date=2020-11-28 |title=The history of mining and mineral exploration in Panama: From Pre-Columbian gold mining to modern copper mining |url=http://boletinsgm.igeolcu.unam.mx/bsgm/vols/epoca04/7203/A180720_Redwood.pdf |journal=Boletín de la Sociedad Geológica Mexicana |volume=72 |issue=3 |article-number=A180720 |doi=10.18268/BSGM2020v72n3a180720 |bibcode=2020BoSGM..72A0720R }} to develop the Santa Rosa gold mine in [[Cañazas]], Panama in 1993.{{Cite journal |last1=Fernández |first1=René R. |last2=Martin |first2=Randy |last3=Bikerman |first3=David |date=April 1997 |title=Managing the Santa Rosa open-pit, heap-leach gold project |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF02914868 |journal=JOM |language=en |volume=49 |issue=4 |pages=15–19 |doi=10.1007/BF02914868 |bibcode=1997JOM....49d..15F |issn=1047-4838|url-access=subscription }} === 1996–2001: financial troubles === [[File:Boliden_Ltd_share_price.svg|thumb|Boliden Ltd's share price collapsed soon after listing in Canada, particularly due to the [[Doñana disaster]] and low metal prices.]] ==== Trelleborg divests Boliden ==== By 1996, Boliden was incurring steep losses, moving Trelleborg to [[Divestment|divest]] Boliden again.{{Cite web |last=Myhr |first=Karin Jansson |date=2025-05-16 |title=Boliden - över 100 år sedan det stora guldfyndet |url=https://www.bizstories.se/foretagen/det-stora-guldfyndet-som-forandrade-allt/ |access-date=2025-07-20 |website=Bizstories |language=sv-SE}} Boliden was restructured as Boliden Limited and reincorporated in Toronto. Trelleborg sold 55% of its shares in Boliden in on the [[Toronto Stock Exchange]] for US${{To USD|875|CAN|year=1997|round=yes}} million ({{Inflation|index=CA|value=0.632|start_year=1997|r=2}} billion today).{{Cite journal |last1=McDermott |first1=Robert K. |last2=Sibley |first2=John M. |date=March 2000 |title=The Aznalcóllar Tailings dam accident—a case study |url=http://www.worldscientific.com/doi/abs/10.1142/S0950609800000111 |journal=Mineral Resources Engineering |language=en |volume=09 |issue=1 |pages=101–118 |doi=10.1142/S0950609800000111 |issn=0950-6098|url-access=subscription }} In 1999, Trelleborg began selling off its remaining 45% stake on the [[Nasdaq Stockholm|Stockholm Stock exchange]];{{Cite web |date=1999-01-25 |title=Trelleborg to participate in new preference issue and to spin off Boliden holding to shareholders |url=https://www.trelleborg.com/media/mfnnews/1999/trelleborg-to-participate-in-new-preference-issue-and-to-spin-off-boliden-holding-to-shareholders |access-date=2025-07-20 |website=www.trelleborg.com |language=en}} by 2001 its stake had been reduced to 8%.{{Cite web |date=2001-12-07 |title=Conversion of preference shares in Boliden |url=https://www.trelleborg.com/en/media/mfnnews/2001/conversion-of-preference-shares-in-boliden |access-date=2025-07-20 |website=www.trelleborg.com |language=en}} Boliden's debts at this time amounted to 8 billion [[Swedish krona|SEK]] ({{Inflation|index=SE|value=8|start_year=2000|r=0}} billion SEK today, or 1.1 billion EUR). ==== Ill-fated acquisition of Westmin ==== In 1997,{{Cite news |date=February 23, 1998 |title=Boliden doubles profits in eventful year |url=https://www.northernminer.com/news/boliden-doubles-profits-in-eventful-year/1000148090/ |work=The Northern Miner}} Boliden Ltd. bought the Canadian company Westmin for {{US dollar|}}{{To USD round|800|CAN|year=1999|sf=2}} million (US${{Inflation|index=US|value=0.540|start_year=1998|r=2}} billion today). Although the acquisition initially appeared a success, with Boliden doubling its profits that year, it quickly became viewed as a disaster. One Canadian newspaper remarked that it had "paid top dollar for a handful of problem mines." Falling metals prices worsened the situation.{{Cite news |date=June 2000 |title=Bulow leaves troubled copper-zinc producer |work=[[Vancouver Sun]]}} By the end of 1998, Boliden was already forced to close one of the acquired mines, the [[Gibraltar Mine|Gibraltar copper mine]] in Canada,{{Cite news |last=Nutt |first=Rod |date=December 15, 1998 |title=Gibraltar will close this week unless bridge financing found |work=Vancouver Sun}} and write off its 51% stake in the unfinished [[Vizcachitas]] copper project in Chile.{{Cite web |date=August 10, 1998 |title=Boliden walks from Vizcachitas joint venture |url=https://northernminer.com/news/boliden-walks-from-vizcachitas-joint-venture/1000162639/ |access-date=2025-07-22 |website=The Northern Miner |language=en-US}} In 1999, it sold the closed Gibraltar mine to [[Taseko Mines|Taseko]] for US$20 million{{Cite web |date=March 31, 2009 |title=Annual Information Form for the fiscal period (15 months) ended December 31, 2008 |url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/878518/000106299309001098/exhibit99-5.htm |access-date=2025-07-22 |website=[[United States Securities and Exchange Commission]]}} and its 50% stake in the Saudi Sukhaybarat gold mine, which it had been co-operating for 8 years,{{Cite news |date=December 20, 1999 |title=Boliden sells stake in Saudi mine. |url=https://www.northernminer.com/news/boliden-sells-stake-in-saudi-mine/1000103312/ |access-date=2025-07-22 |work=The Northern Miner}} for {{US dollar|6.9}} million.{{Cite journal |date=1999-12-20 |title=Saudi Arabia's Ma'adin Buys Out Boliden From Gold Mine Venture |url=http://archives.mees.com/issues/669/articles/26780 |journal=[[Middle East Economic Survey]] |volume=42 |issue=51}} In 2004, Boliden sold what remained of its Westmin assets to [[Breakwater Resources]] for US${{To USD round|42|SWE|sf=2|year=2004}} million in company shares.{{Cite press release |last=Boliden |date=2004-07-08 |title=Boliden's Myra Falls mine now sold |url=https://www.globenewswire.com/fr/news-release/2004/07/08/312858/1316/en/Boliden-s-Myra-Falls-mine-now-sold.html |access-date=2025-07-22 |website=GlobeNewswire News Room |language=en}} ==== Doñana disaster ==== {{Main|Doñana disaster}} On 25 April 1998, the [[tailings dam]] at Apirsa's Los Frailes mine burst and 4.5 million cubic metres of [[tailings]] sand drained out into the nearby [[Guadiamar]] river, near [[Doñana National Park]], causing Spain's worst environmental disaster in modern history. The dam's failure was attributed to gradual deterioration of its [[marl]] foundation in contact with the acidic contents of the dam. Although the company claimed [[force majeure]], critics noted that issues with the foundation had been identified two years previously.{{Citation |last1=Shahriari |first1=M. |chapter=Lessons Learned from Analysis of Los Frailes Tailing Dam Failure |date=2018 |title=Advances in Safety Management and Human Factors |volume=604 |pages=309–317 |editor-last=Arezes |editor-first=Pedro |chapter-url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-3-319-60525-8_32 |access-date=2025-07-20 |place=Cham |publisher=Springer International Publishing |doi=10.1007/978-3-319-60525-8_32 |isbn=978-3-319-60524-1 |last2=Aydin |first2=M. E.|chapter-url-access=subscription }} The company closed the mine permanently and began [[Stream restoration|reclamation]] work. The financial cost of the disaster wiped out Boliden's profits. As a result, its share price also dropped sharply.{{Cite web |date=2000-05-22 |title=Boliden expands Ronnskar |url=https://www.northernminer.com/news/boliden-expands-ronnskar/1000103971/ |access-date=2025-07-20 |website=The Northern Miner |language=en-US}} Although the company was cleared of criminal responsibility in 2001, the Spanish government fined Boliden's Spanish subsidiary, which had already gone bankrupt, €45 million (€{{Inflation|index=ES|value=43.7|start_year=1999|r=1}} million today) in 2002.{{Cite news |date=2002-08-03 |title=Spain fines toxic spill firm $45m |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/2170020.stm |access-date=2025-07-20 |work=[[BBC News]] |language=en-GB}} Boliden unsuccessfully sued several of the construction companies that had built the dam.{{cite news |url=https://elpais.com/diario/2006/11/25/andalucia/1164410528_850215.html |title=Boliden Apirsa pierde la demanda contra las empresas que hicieron la balsa de Aznalcóllar | work=[[El País]] |date=24 November 2006 | language=Spanish}} The [[Environmental remediation|remediation]] costs of Aznalcóllar ended up costing €240 million (€{{Inflation|index=ES|value=240|start_year=2001|r=0}} million today).{{Cite web |last=Venna |first=Srivani |date=2015-05-17 |title=Spain postpones reopening controversial Aznalcóllar mine amid bribery allegations |url=https://www.mining-technology.com/marketdata/newsspain-halts-reopening-controversial-aznalcllar-mine-bribery-allegations-4579418/ |access-date=2025-07-22 |website=Mining Technology |language=en-US}} === 2001–present: re-focusing on Europe === In 2001, Boliden was redomiciled in Sweden as Boliden AB.{{Cite news |year=2001 |title=Boliden announces shareholder approval of redomiciliation to Sweden |url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/vprr/0200/02002647.pdf |work=Canada News Wire}} The company began pivoting back to its European roots. In 2000, it invested US$245 million in an expansion of [[Rönnskär]], its biggest smelting plant, which had been a reliable source of revenue throughout the difficult 1990s. The expansion, consisting of more energy-efficient [[Flash smelting|flash furnaces]], was expected to pay for itself within 7 years. New exploration and development efforts followed in northern Sweden, including the [[Maurliden]] zinc mine (opened in 2001){{Cite book |last=Andersson |first=Elin |url=https://urn.kb.se/resolve?urn=urn:nbn:se:ltu:diva-46698 |title=A Laboratory Study of ARD Neutralization and Prevention by Alkaline Rest Products: Waste rock from Maurliden |date=September 2012 |publisher=Luleå University of Technology |language=en}} and the [[Storliden]] copper/zinc mine (opened in 2002).{{Cite web |last=Schuster |first=Thomas |title=Sweden's Storliden makes the grade |url=https://secure.northernminer.com/news/sweden-s-storliden-makes-the-grade/1000149490/ |access-date=2025-07-22 |website=The Northern Miner |language=en-US}} In 2004, Boliden sold Storliden to Lundin Mining for 123 million SEK ({{Inflation|index=SE|value=123|start_year=2004|r=0}} million SEK today, or 16 million EUR).{{Cite web |last=Radio |first=Sveriges |date=2004-12-31 |title=Boliden säljer sina aktier i NAN - P4 Västerbotten |url=https://www.sverigesradio.se/artikel/531053 |access-date=2025-07-22 |website=www.sverigesradio.se |language=sv}} In 2003, Boliden further narrowed its focus on mining and refining by swapping its advanced manufacturing and sales units{{Cite journal |date=2003-12-09 |title=Tema: Koppar |url=https://resource.sgu.se/dokument/publikation/pp/pp200305rapport/pp2003-5-rapport.pdf |journal=Mineralmarknaden |publisher=[[Geological Survey of Sweden]] |volume=34 |page=32}} for [[Outokumpu|Outokumpu's]] mining and smelting assets.{{cite press release | url=https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2003/10/25/302172/1316/en/Boliden-and-Outokumpu-sign-final-agreement-to-create-a-world-leading-mining-and-smelting-company-New-Boliden.html |title=Boliden and Outokumpu sign final agreement to create a | publisher=[[GlobeNewswire]] | date=October 25, 2003}} The deal included the [[Tara Mine|Tara zinc mine]] in Ireland; zinc smelters in [[Kokkola]] (Finland) and [[Odda (town)|Odda]] (Norway); and copper smelting and refining operations in [[Harjavalta]] and [[Pori]] (Finland). In exchange, Outokumpu acquired Boliden's brass and other downstream units. To partially fund the transaction, Boliden issued new shares, resulting in Outokumpu owning 49% of the company. Outokumpu gradually sold off its stake over the next three years.{{Cite web |date=2005-09-20 |title=Outokumpu has sold the remaining shares in Boliden |url=https://investors.boliden.com/en/press/outokumpu-has-sold-remaining-shares-boliden-1022399 |access-date=2025-07-22 |website=Boliden |language=en}} In 2006, Boliden approved a $790 million (${{Inflation|index=SE|value=0.790|start_year=2006|r=1}} billion today) expansion of its [[Aitik|Aitik copper mine]], which was completed in 2010.{{Cite web |title=Boliden Copper Mine, Aitik, Sweden |url=https://www.mining-technology.com/projects/aitik/ |access-date=2025-07-23 |website=Mining Technology |language=en-US}} That same year, [[OM Group]] signed a 3-year contract for Boliden to refine 240,000 tons of nickel [[Ore concentrate|concentrate]] annually at its Harjavalta smelter.{{Cite web |date=2006-02-03 |title=Boliden ökar nickelsmältningen i Finland |url=https://www.svt.se/nyheter/lokalt/vasterbotten/boliden-okar-nickelsmaltningen-i-finland |access-date=2025-07-24 |website=SVT Nyheter |language=sv}} Successful exploration resulted in increases to Garpenberg's ore reserves. A new lead section was also opened at Bergsöe. In 2016, Boliden purchased the [[Kevitsa mine]] in Finland for{{Cite web |title=Svensk Verkstad |url=https://svenskverkstad.se/ |access-date=2025-07-24 |website=Svensk Verkstad |language=sv}} for US$712 million.{{Cite web |date=2016-06-01 |title=Bolidens förvärv av gruvan Kevitsa slutfört |url=https://news.cision.com/se/boliden/r/bolidens-forvarv-av-gruvan-kevitsa-slutfort,c2021615 |access-date=2025-07-24 |website=Cision |language=sv}} In 2016, Boliden was ranked as being among the 13th best of 92 oil, gas, and mining companies on indigenous rights in the Arctic.{{Cite web |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/313474088 | title=Ranking Oil, Gas and Mining Companies on Indigenous Rights in the Arctic | last=Overland | first=Indra | via=[[ResearchGate]] | work=[[Norwegian Institute of International Affairs]] |date=December 2016}} In April 2025, Boliden acquired Somnicor, owner of the [[Neves-Corvo mine]], and Zinkgruvan mine from [[Lundin Mining]] for US$1.4 billion plus up to an additional US$150 million in contingency payments.{{Cite press release | url=https://lundinmining.com/news/lundin-mining-completes-the-sale-of-neves-corvo-an-123194/ | title=Lundin Mining Completes the Sale of Neves-Corvo and Zinkgruvan to Boliden | publisher=[[Lundin Mining]] | date=April 16, 2025}} ==Waste dumping disaster in Chile== In the mid-1980s, allegedly to circumvent stricter environmental laws in Sweden, Boliden offloaded around 19,000 tonnes of waste to Promel, a Chilean company, for processing. Boliden paid 10 million SEK for Promel to take on the waste. The waste had been stored in Boliden's Rönnskär smelter for several decades{{Cite web |last=Lamm |first=Susanne |date=2016-11-18 |title=Johan Öberg driver unikt rättsfall mot Boliden |url=https://www.epochtimes.se/johan-oberg-driver-unikt-rattsfall-mot-boliden |access-date=2025-07-15 |website=Svenska Epoch Times |language=sv}} and contained high concentrations of hazardous elements, including [[arsenic]], [[Mercury (element)|mercury]], [[cadmium]] and [[lead]].{{cite web |date=23 March 2023 |title=Joint Communication from Special Procedures |url=https://www.boliden.com/globalassets/sustainability/our-responsibilities/in-focus/questions-from-un.pdf |website=boliden.com}} Promel claimed to want to extract and sell the gold contained in the waste, but never ended up doing so. The waste was, instead, stored on the outskirts of the city of [[Arica]], at a site which was converted to a low-cost residential area in the 1990s on the instructions of the social services. The original export documents had claimed that the metallic residues were 'non-toxic' and residents were unaware of the waste's presence or potential for harm. However, in the late 1990s and early 2000s, reports began emerging of people suffering from symptoms consistent with [[arsenic poisoning]].{{Cite web |last1=Sear |first1=Laura |last2=Steed |first2=Leslie |date=2019-04-12 |title=Swedish waste poisons Chilean community |url=https://www.dw.com/en/swedish-toxic-waste-poisons-chilean-community-for-30-years/a-51424782 |access-date=2025-07-16 |website=DW |language=en}} By 2008, 12,000 people were believed to be affected.{{Cite web |last=Rocksén |first=Andreas |date=2024-11-07 |title=Nytt avtal ger hopp åt dem som drabbats av Bolidens gifter |url=https://da.se/2024/11/nytt-avtal-ger-hopp-at-dem-som-drabbats-av-bolidens-gifter/ |access-date=2025-07-16 |website=Dagens Arbete |language=sv-SE}} In 2009, the Chilean government evacuated around 7,000 residents of the area. The waste was exported before the [[Basel Convention]] prohibiting the export of environmentally hazardous waste came into force. [[File:Presidente de la República, Gabriel Boric Font, sostiene reunión bilateral con el Primer Ministro de Suecia, Ulf Kristersson.jpg|thumb|At a meeting in 2024, Chilean president [[Gabriel Boric]] and Swedish prime minister [[Ulf Kristersson]] committed to cleaning up the mining waste Boliden had sold to a Chilean company in 1985.]] In 2013, 700 Chilean victims of arsenic poisoning filed a lawsuit against Boliden.{{cite web |title=Boliden lawsuit (re Chile) |url=https://www.business-humanrights.org/en/latest-news/boliden-lawsuit-re-chile/ |website=Business & Human Rights Resource Centre | date=12 Sep 2013}}{{cite news |title=Swedish mining company sued for poisoning in Chile |url=https://www.sverigesradio.se/artikel/5646871 | work=[[Sveriges Radio]] |date=16 September 2013}} The plaintiffs lost the case in the Skellefteå [[District courts of Sweden|district court]] in 2019. Their appeal to the [[Courts of appeal in Sweden|appeals court]] was also rejected the following year; the court found that the [[statute of limitations]] of 10 years had run out.{{Cite web |last=Forsman |first=Karin |date=2025-09-03 |title=Inget skadestånd för påstådd miljöskada i Chile på 1980-talet |url=https://www.jpinfonet.se/kunskap/nyheter4/inget-skadestand-for-pastadd-miljoskada-i-chile-pa-1980-talet/ |access-date=2025-07-15 |website=JP Infonet |language=sv}} In 2024, during a [[state visit]] to Sweden, Chilean president [[Gabriel Boric]] discussed the issue with Swedish prime minister [[Ulf Kristersson]]. The pair signed a [[letter of intent]] promising to cooperate on the removal of mining waste.{{Cite web |last=Staffan |first=Lindberg |date=2024-10-15 |title=Sverige och Chile ska samarbeta för att få bort giftavfall |url=https://www.aftonbladet.se/a/B0kz79 |access-date=2025-07-15 |website=[[Aftonbladet]] |language=sv}} The decades-long disaster led to widespread criticism of Boliden and Sweden. Boliden was criticized for its intransigence in dealing with the victims. The Swedish state was also accused of showing excessive deference to the company and not following its own laws on the export of hazardous waste.{{Cite news |last=Orellana |first=Marcos |date=2021-05-27 |title="Sverige måste ta ansvar för giftskandal i Chile" |url=https://www.svd.se/a/561y9W/sverige-maste-ta-ansvar-for-giftskandal-i-chile |access-date=2025-07-16 |work=Svenska Dagbladet |language=sv |issn=1101-2412}} The journalist [[Marcos A. Orellana|Marcos Orellana]], serving as a [[United Nations Special Rapporteur on Toxics and Human Rights|United Nations special rapporteur]], investigated the case and wrote that he "could not imagine" he would be writing about Sweden when he accepted his job. He deplored Boliden's tactics of casting doubt on the validity of the arsenic poisoning cases and urged both Boliden and the Swedish government to finally acknowledge their role in the disaster, "remedy the damage caused to the population of Arica," and arrange for the waste to be stored in Boliden's purpose-built repository at its Rönnskärsverken site in Sweden. ==Human rights record== In September 2020, Boliden lawyers sued lawyers Johan Öberg and Göran Starkebo, who were representing the alleged Chilean victims of arsenic poisoning from Boliden's waste dumping scandal in the 1980s. Boliden attempted to make them personally liable for costs incurred by Boliden in defending the case.{{Cite web |title=Boliden lawsuit (Re Chile) |url=https://www.business-humanrights.org/en/latest-news/boliden-lawsuit-re-chile/}} It was considered by [[Annalisa Ciampi]], who was serving as a [[United Nations special rapporteur|UN special rapporteur]], to be an [[Strategic lawsuit against public participation|intimidation lawsuit]].{{Cite web |title=Info Note |url=https://www.ohchr.org/Documents/Issues/FAssociation/InfoNoteSLAPPsFoAA.docx |via=ohchr.org}} ==Environmental record== One of Boliden's mines, the Los Frailes mine near Sevilla, was the site of one of Spain's [[Doñana disaster|worst environmental disasters]] in modern history in 1998.{{Cite news |last=McKie |first=Robin |date=2014-04-26 |title=Spain's wetlands wonder is under threat for a second time in 16 years |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2014/apr/27/spanish-wildlife-park-under-threat |access-date=2025-07-16 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}{{Cite news | url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg15821321-900-donana-damned/ |last=McKenzie |first=Deborah | title=Doñana damned | work=[[New Scientist]] | date=May 2, 1998}} In 2017, Boliden was rated the world's second most climate-friendly mining firm with regards to carbon dioxide.{{cite web | url=https://www.wemeanbusinesscoalition.org/blog/digging-deep-miners-facing-low-carbon-challenge/ | title=Digging deep: Which miners are facing up to the low-carbon challenge? | website=We Mean Business | date=July 6, 2017}} In August 2021, Boliden was one of several major mining companies to join [[Komatsu Limited|Komatsu]] to advance zero-emission mining.{{cite news | url=https://www.mining-technology.com/news/rio-tinto-bhp-komatsus-alliance/ | title=Rio Tinto and BHP join Komatsu's alliance for zero-emission mining | last=Rani |first=Archana | date=August 3, 2021 | website=Mining Technology | publisher=Verdict Media}} In August 2021, Boliden ranked second among mining companies in Bloomberg Intelligence's low-carbon ranking.{{cite web |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-08-17/most-miners-are-falling-short-of-carbon-cuts-needed-for-un-goal/ |title=Most Miners Are Falling Short of Carbon Cuts Needed for UN Goal | work=[[Bloomberg News]] |date=August 17, 2021}} In 2021, Boliden was ranked no. 18 out of 120 oil, gas, and mining companies involved in resource extraction north of the Arctic Circle in the Arctic Environmental Responsibility Index (AERI).Overland, I., Bourmistrov, A., Dale, B., Irlbacher-Fox, S., Juraev, J., Podgaiskii, E., Stammler, F., Tsani, S., Vakulchuk, R. and Wilson, E.C. 2021. Boliden AB (stylized as Boliden) is a Swedish multinational metals, mining, and smelting company headquartered in Stockholm. The company produces zinc, copper, lead, nickel, silver, and gold, with operations in Sweden, Finland, Norway, Portugal, and Ireland.
Founded in the 1920s and named after the Boliden mine, a now-defunct gold mine 30 km northwest of the Swedish town of Skellefteå, Boliden AB began as a gold mining company. Over the following decades, it expanded into copper, silver and nickel mining, as well as smelting. In the 1970s, following a period of high metals prices, the company diversified aggressively, purchasing appliance manufacturers, wholesalers and trading companies. In 1985, it was acquired by Trelleborg, a polymer manufacturer, which refocused it back on mining while also expanding overseas. In 1998, Trelleborg moved Boliden's headquarters to Toronto, Canada and sold Boliden again on the stock market. However, Boliden's share price collapsed over the next four years, due to a combination of low metal prices and a dam failure at one of its mines in Spain that led to an environmental disaster. In 2002, it moved its headquarters back to Sweden, sold off its non-European assets and regained profitability.
Boliden owns and operates Europe's biggest zinc mine at Tara in Ireland (acquired in 2004). Boliden also owns Garpenberg, a zinc-lead mine and Sweden's oldest mine still in operation. The mineral-rich Skellefte field lies within the Boliden Area, where almost 30 mines have been opened since production began in the 1920s and where Boliden currently operates the Renström and Kristineberg underground mines and the Maurliden open pit mine. Boliden also owns and operates the Aitik copper mine.
Boliden refines both metal concentrate and scrap waste at its smelters in Sweden, Finland and Norway to produce base metals and precious metals. Its main metals are zinc and copper, but the production of lead, gold and silver also makes a substantial contribution to its revenues. It is also a significant producer of sulfuric acid as a refining byproduct.
